observations_recorded_at_seal.NO_GATE_HERE_CAN_PASS_TRIVIALLY_AND_THAT: The text states it outright: 'every control gates on a POSITIVE prediction it can miss; nothing is satisfiable by a dead apparatus (a fully depolarized flight fails G1, G2, G4a simultaneously).' This is the direct answer to what I recorded on H10-C2 hours earlier — there G2 PASSED trivially because everything read zero, and I logged that its pass carried NO independent weight. Here the health gates are BANDS with a floor: a dead apparatus reads ~0.62 and FAILS G4a/G4b rather than sailing through. A control that cannot fail is not a control, and this prereg is built so none of them can be satisfied by wash.
observations_recorded_at_seal.THE_DEPTH_BAR_IS_STATED_PRE_TRANSPILE: 150 2q gates against a ~110 estimate, with the bar written down BEFORE the transpiler runs — same discipline as C2, where the estimate was stated up front and the transpiler's actual number given the deciding vote. A hold set after seeing the number is not a hold.
observations_recorded_at_seal.CHEAPEST_FLIGHT_ON_THE_BOARD: 3-6 QPU-s. For scale: C1's pilot cost 12 QPU-s to return NO-FLY and C2 cost ~60 to return DOES NOT HOLD. This one is cheaper than either negative, and its bars are Elder's already-computed ceilings rather than new estimates.

This is the C2-G2 lesson one level sharper: there a control could not fail at all; here it could fail, but not against the fault most likely to occur.

Depth ~8 2q gates against the 190 that tripped the hold.
amendment_3.registered_value_change: parallel 0.865308 (joint rotation) -> 6/7 = 0.857143 EXACT. The joint rotation bought only 0.008 over the product optimum. The flown staircase is now all exact fractions: switch 15/21 < parallel 18/21 < flip 1.
amendment_3.WHY_THE_SUBSET_RULE_DOES_NOT_APPLY_HERE_: Subset-of-every-predecessor governs BAND EDITS AT A FIXED INSTRUMENT. This is an INSTRUMENT CHANGE, so the bands are RE-DERIVED from the paired rule rather than tightened, and the anti-gaming audit becomes GATE-BY-GATE. Whisper scoped this explicitly in the amendment text rather than quietly applying subset logic where it does not fit — which is the correct handling and the reason I could verify it at all.

THE_CHECK_THAT_ACTUALLY_MATTERS_FOR_A_HE.question: Does the loosened band admit any KNOWN FAULT VALUE?
THE_CHECK_THAT_ACTUALLY_MATTERS_FOR_A_HE.result: PASS — no known fault value lies in (0.87, 0.89]. A dead apparatus (~0.62), the computed single faults (31/42 = 0.738095), the switch ideal (5/7) and the flip ideal (1.0) ALL still FAIL G4a. The gate remains POSITIVE AND MISSABLE, which is the property the band exists to have. This assertion is enforced in the sealing script — the entry cannot be written if a fault value falls inside.
THE_CHECK_THAT_ACTUALLY_MATTERS_FOR_A_HE.why_this_is_the_right_test: 'Narrower' was never the point; the point is whether anything that SHOULD fail can now pass. For a health band the subset rule is a cheap PROXY for that, and where the proxy and the real question disagree, the real question governs — but only when the real question is answered MECHANICALLY, as here, against an enumerated fault set fixed before the data exists. That is the difference between re-deriving a bound and rationalising one.

Elder raised this one as UNVERIFIED rather than as a defect, and declined to press it further pre-flight because he could not certify the seesaw either way — then converted it into a blind landing-time rule that CANNOT rescue a failure. A co-checker who only reports confirmed defects teaches the room that a flag means guilt.

amendment_5.what_it_fixes: The graded-EXPLORATORY flight failed its own registered KA fence: NO registered reading cleared it (registered referent 0.865308 + 1e-9 -> fails 8.2e6x; corrected referent 6/7 + registered 1e-9 -> fails 140x; corrected referent + FLOWN 1e-6 -> passes, and was never registered). Cause: the fence's target constants were 6-DECIMAL LITERALS of exact fractions. |6/7 - 0.857143| = 1.4286e-7 and |15/21 - 0.714286| = 2.8571e-7 reproduced the observed residuals EXACTLY. The walker was accurate to float64; the constant it was graded against was accurate to six places.
